falsepos.message:
Basis1D: segment 1 of this NON-UNIFORM element grid is 8.33335e-10 wide -- 8.333e-04 of the period 1e-06, below the minimum 1e-03 this basis contracts for (walls [0.000000e+00 4.995833e-07 5.004167e-07 1.000000e-06]).
  WHY.  The staggered stiffness carries the per-segment 1/J_n (Granet Eq. 31), so a segment this narrow carries spurious modal wavenumbers |gamma| ~ 1.07e+03 x G (G = 2 pi / period) -- modes oscillating that many times per period, against the handful a physical mode of this cell can.  Inside one grid they are harmless; across an L2 MORTAR (layer_grids='per-layer' with neighbours on other grids) the cross-grid projection conditions as 1/w^2 on the E row and 1/w^3.2 on the H row, and the damage is ENERGY-INVISIBLE -- the lossless closure stays pinned, so no tripwire fires.  MEASURED: a device that cannot depend on this wall separation at all reads a 3.4-5.4x FLOOR under its n_modes ladder (docs/audits/FIX_PMM2D_MORTAR_ROUND2_2026_09_11.md).
  REMEDIES.  (1) MERGE the two walls -- a feature this fine is below what the method resolves; (2) carry the fine feature on the SHARED lattice (PMM2DStackPure(..., layer_grids='shared') with an N that resolves it), where every cell is period/N and this cannot form; (3) use PMM2DStackHybrid, which is Fourier-projected and has no element grid; (4) on a TAPER, lower n_slices or stop the taper before its tip closes (the midpoint rule's narrowest sampled width is ~w_bottom / (2 n_slices)).  Raising n_modes is NOT a remedy: the spurious spectrum grows as M (M + 1).
